name: Pale Glaucous-Green
lede: Pale Glaucous-Green is a pale, greenish white from Ridgway's 1912 plates, measured in our color graph as identical to a separately sourced Pale Sage, and most loved by Paul Signac.

sections.title: A near-white green, named twice
sections.body:
*Glaucous* describes a pale bluish or greyish green, like the bloom on a grape, and Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* places this hue at plate XXXIII, hue 39′′, tone f, scanned from an aged plate and so approximate [1]. The ISCC-NBS system later filed it in its own block, classifying it as a greenish white [1]. Our color graph finds a separately recorded name, Pale Sage, at zero units of difference, an exact duplicate under a different name [2].

Its nearest distinct relatives in the graph are [[pale-niagara-green]], greener, and [[grey-white]] and [[pale-olivine]], close behind [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, a color within six units of Pale Glaucous-Green covers at least five per cent of a canvas in 421 works, more common than 76 per cent of our named colors [4]. The painter most devoted to it is Paul Signac, in 5 of his 18 works here, about 6.1 times his museums' baseline [4]. It most often shares a canvas with [[charcoal-grey]] and [[leek-green]], at 5.0 and 4.2 times the expected rate [4]. The earliest dated appearance in our archive is 1256, over six centuries before the name's own 1912 record, a look-alike hue, not proof of pigment, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [4]. These remain photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors [4].
